Earnings per share
The earnings considered in ascertaining the Company's Earnings per share (EPS) comprise of the Net

Profit/Loss after tax. The number of shares used for computing the basic EPS is the weighted average
number of shares outstanding during the year.

Dilutive potential equity shares are deemed to have been converted as of the beginning of the year, unless
they have been issued at a later date. The number of shares used in computing diluted EPS comprises of
weighted average number of shares considered for deriving basic EPS, and also the weighted average
number of equity shares which could have been issued to the conversion of all dilutive potential equity
shares where avplicable.

Employee benefits

Retirement benefit in the form of Provident Fund is a defined contribution scheme and the contributions
are charged to the Statement of Profit and Loss for the year when the contributions to the respective funds
are due. There are no other obligations other than the Provident Fund Contribution.

Gratuity

Gratuity is a post-employment benefit and is a defined benefit obligation. The liability recognised in the
Balance Sheet represents the present value of the defined benefit obligation at the Balance Sheet date less
the fair value of the plan assets, together with adjustments for unrecognised actuarial gains or losses and
past service costs. Independent actuary using the projected unit credit method calculated the defined
benefit obligations annually.

Actuarial gains or losses arising from experience adjustments and changes in actuary assumptions are
credited or charged to the statement of profit and loss in the year in which such gains or losses arises.

Cash Flow Statement

Cash flows are reported using the indirect method, whereby profit / (loss) before extraordinary items and
tax is adjusted for the effects of transactions of non-cash nature and any deferrals or accruals of past or
future cash receipts or payments. The cash flow from operating, investing and financing activities of the
group are segregated based on the available information.

Cash and cash equivalents (for the purpose of Cash Flow Statement)
Cash comprise cash on hand and demand deposits with banks. Cash equivalents are short term balances
(with an original maturity of three months or less from the date of acquisition), highly liquid investments

that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash and which are subject to insignificant risk of
chanoes in value

. Lease transactions

The payments made by the Company as lessee in accordance with operational leasing contracts or rental
agreements are expensed proportionally during the lease or rental period respectively.

Provisions and Contingencies

Provisions involving substantial degree of estimation in measurement are recognized when there is a
present obligation as a result of past events and it is probable that there will be an outflow of resources.
Contingent liabilities are not recognized but disclosed in the notes. Contingent Assets are neither
recognized nor disclosed in the financial statements.

General

The Accounting policies not specifically referred to are in accordance with generally accepted accounting
policies.

WHEREAS: 
 
1. M/s. ILab’s Hyderabad Techonology Centre Private Limited, having its registered office at 
iLabs Centre, Unit 18, Building 3, Software Units Layout, Madhapur, Hyderabad 500081 
(“Lessor”) is the sole, absolute and lawful owner of the land and building situated at Plot 
No. 18, SurveyNo.64 (p) Madhapur, Serilingampally Mandal, Rangareddy District, 
comprised in iLabs Centre measuring a total extent of 5.56Acres, having acquired the same 
by the way of Deed of Sale dated 15th February, 2006 and registered as document No. 
4295/06 with the District Registrar’s Office, Ranga Reddy District, for the establishment of 
Information Technology Park iLabs Centre as more particularly described in Schedule A 
hereunder (“the said iLabs Centre”). 
 
2. The Sub-Lessor had executed a Principal Lease Deed (“Principal Lease Deed”) with the 
Lessor whereby the Lessor had granted the premises measuring 5,700 sq. ft. (super built-up 
area), on the 8thFloor, D Block of the iLabs Centre which is  located at the Plot No.18, 
Software Units lay-out, carved out of Survey No.64 (p), Madhapur, Hyderbad-500081, 
India, more particularly described under Schedule B (“Leased Premises”) 
 
3. Pursuant to the Principal Lease Deed, the Leased Premises has been granted on lease by the 
Lessor to the Sub-Lessor for a period of sixty (60) months commencing from 1st February 
2023 till 31st January 2028 subject to a renewal of forty-eight (48) months at the option of 
the Sub-Lessor.  
 
4. The Sub-Lesse is now desirous of taking 1,950 sq. ft. out of 5,700 sq. ft. (viz. a portion of 
the Leased Premises) on sub-lease. The Sub-Lessor has agreed to let out the premises 
measuring 1,950 sq. ft. (super built-up area), on the 8thFloor, D Block of the iLabs Centre 
which is located at the Plot No.18, Software Units lay-out, carved out of Survey No.64 (p), 
Madhapur, Hyderbad-500081, India, more particularly described as Schedule C (“Demised 
Premises”) to the Sub-Lessee on the terms and conditions set forth hereinafter, and Sub-
Lessee shall use and occupy the Demised Premises solely for the purpose mentioned in 
Article V(b) hereunder and for no other purpose unless the Sub-Lessor shall expressly 
approve of such use in advance in writing. 
 
NOW THIS DEED WITNESSETH AS FOLLOWS: 
 
ARTICLE.I-TERM 
 
(a) 
In consideration of the monthly rent and other terms and conditions agreed upon and 
hereinafter stipulated, the Sub- Lessor hereby grants and the Sub-Lessee hereby accepts 
from the Sub-Lessor, lease of the Demised Premises for a period of 60 months (“Sub-
Lease Period”) commencing from 1st February, 2023 (“Commencement Date”) till 31st 
January 2028 both days inclusive, subject to any extension as specified under Article 
I(b). The Sub-Lessor shall ensure that the Sub-Lessee has a peaceful vacant possession 
of the Demised Premises, and no hindrance is caused to the Sub-Lessee during the Sub-
Lease Period and any such renewal. 
 
Page 3 of 23 
 
 
(b) 
This Deed may be renewed for one additional period of 48 months (the “Extended 
Term”) after the expiration of the Sub-Lease Period at the option of the Sub-Lessee on 
the terms and conditions mutually agreed including escalation as mentioned in Article 
II(b). The Sub-Lessee shall issue a notice to the Sub-Lessor in writing of the Sub-Lessee’s 
intention to renew the lease at least 90 days prior to the expiry of the Sub-Lease Period. 
On renewal, the Parties shall execute a fresh Deed and the Sub-Lessee shall have it 
adequately stamped and registered. 
 
(c) 
There shall be a lock-in period of 33 months from 1st February 2023 (“Lock-in Period”) 
during which time neither Party shall be entitled to terminate the Deed except (i) in case 
of a breach of the terms of this Deed by either Party; or (ii) a force majeure event as 
mentioned under Article XXII. Pursuant to the expiration of the Lock-in Period, Sub-
Lessee may terminate this Deed by serving an advance notice of 90 days to the Sub-
Lessor.  
ARTICLE.II-SUB-LEASE RENT 
 
(a) The Lessee agrees to pay the lease rent for the warm shell of the Demised Premises at 
the rate of Rs.64/- (Rupees Sixty-Four only) per sq. ft. per month for the total area of 
the Demised Premises (viz. 1,950 sq. ft.) taken on sub-lease amounting to a total sub-
lease rent of Rs. 1,24,800/- (One Lakh Twenty-Four Thousand and Eight Hundred 
Only) per month plus GST as applicable subject to deduction of applicable taxes at 
source as required by applicable law (“Rent”), and the same shall be paid in advance 
by cheque payable on or before the 7th day of each calendar month.  
 
(b) The Rent would include high side power upto the tapping point, 100% power back up 
provisions, common area flooring, and electric cables up to the Demised Premises. 
All taxes, cesses, rates, levies, outgoings, charges, etc. are payable by the Sub-Lessor 
to any association or any other public authority and any other charges in respect to the 
Demised Premises except as agreed under this Deed. All other future taxes, levied by 
any governmental / statutory authority (excluding direct taxes on the income of the 
Sub-Lessor or taxes related to or in connection with ownership of the land/unit by the 
Lessor) in relation to this Deed for the lease of the Demised Premises shall be to the 
account of the Sub-Lessee, and all such other future taxes, levied by any such 
governmental/ statutory authority in relation to the maintenance of the common areas, 
shall also be to the account of the Sub-Lessee, at Sub-Lessee’s pro-rata share. The 
payment of Rent in respect of the Demised Premises shall commence from 1st July 
2023. 
 
(c) The Rent shall be subject to an escalation of 5% every year. The first escalation will 
be on 1st February 2024 followed by 5% escalation every 12 months. 
 
(d) All rental payments shall be addressed to Sub-Lessor at the address set forth in the 
description of Parties of this Deed, or at such other place as the Sub-Lessor may 
from time to time designate by an advance written notice of one month to the Sub-
Lessee. The terms and provisions of this Article shall survive the expiration or 
termination of this Deed in relation to all sums due and payable and which remains 
unpaid at the time of termination of this Deed.  
 
 
 
 
Page 4 of 23 
 
 
(e) The rent per sq. ft. for the Demised Premises does not include electricity charges, 
interest on delayed payment, if any, charges for using facilities in commercial areas 
in the said iLabs Centre (other than the Demised Premises for Sub-Lessee’s 
activities), or other charges specifically payable by the Sub-Lessee under this Deed, 
and shall only be payable and due by the Sub-Lessee from time to time as agreed in 
writing between the Parties. Except for the Security Deposit, Rent, service tax and 
charges specifically stated in this Deed as payable by the Sub-Lessee, the Sub-
Lessee shall not be liable to pay any amounts to the Sub-Lessor for the possession 
and enjoyment of the Demised Premises under this Deed.  
 
(f) The Sub-Lessee shall be charged for electricity on a proportionate basis, i.e., 15% 
of the total electricity bill of the premises will be paid by Sub-Lessee. Any additional 
costs (inclusive of all taxes and levies as may be applicable) incurred by the Sub-
Lessor on account of any additional specifications provided at the Sub-Lessee’s 
request, relating to the Demised Premises, including but not limited to additional 
power requirements or air conditioning specifications shall be borne by the Sub-
Lessee. The Sub-Lessee shall own, possess and control any equipment or machinery 
acquired and installed, if any, where payment in respect of such equipment or 
machinery has been borne by the Sub-Lessee.  
 
ARTICLE.III-SECURITY DEPOSIT 
 
(a) 
On the Commencement Date, the Sub-Lessee shall deposit a refundable interest-free 
security deposit of Rs.7,48,800/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Forty-Eight Thousand and Eight 
Hundred only) equivalent to 6 months of Rent as “Security Deposit”.  
 
(b) 
On the expiry or earlier termination of this Deed, the Sub-Lessor shall refund the Security 
Deposit to the Sub-Lessee upon vacating and handing over the vacant and peaceful 
possession of the Demised Premises. The Parties shall settle and pay the outstanding 
amounts within 30 days from the day the Sub-Lessee vacates the premises and informs 
the Sub-Lessor of the same as provided in this Deed through execution of sub-lease 
termination agreement laying down total Security Deposit held, dues payable by lessee, 
damages and adjustments and balance refundable to lessee.  
(c) 
Upon expiry or termination of this Deed, if the Sub-Lessor fails to refund to the Sub-
Lessee the total Security Deposit, the Sub-Lessee shall be entitled to remain in occupation 
and possession of the Demised Premises till such time the Security Deposit and the Power 
Consumption is refunded without paying any Rent or any other amounts.  Such staying 
over by the Sub-Lessee in the Demised Premises shall not constitute a default by the Sub-
Lessee under the terms hereof nor will the Sub-Lessee be an unauthorized occupant of the 
Demised Premises. Notwithstanding the aforesaid, it is expressly recorded and mutually 
agreed that this clause or anything else to the contrary, does not and shall not be construed 
or deemed to extend the Sub-Lease Period and shall survive the termination of this Deed. 
 
ARTICLE.IV-OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE SERVICES 
 
(a) 
The Sub-Lessor is under an obligation to maintain common areas and provide certain 
amenities, facilities and services in discharge of its obligation, more particularly described 
under Schedule D (“Operation and Maintenance Services”). 
Page 5 of 23 
 
 
(b) 
Without prejudice to the Sub-Lessor’s sole obligation to render such services, the Sub-
Lessor shall be entitled to engage any person and/or entity under contract from time to 
time in order to provide services to the Sub-Lessee. 
(c) 
In addition to the Rent and Security Deposit and Power Consumption Deposit amounts 
payable by the Sub-Lessee to the Sub-Lessor as mentioned herein above, the Sub-Lessee 
shall pay an amount of Rs.11.60  (Rupees Eleven and Sixty Paise only) per sq. ft. per 
month as operation and maintenance fee for the sub-leased area of 1,950 Sq. ft. amounting 
to Rs.22,620/- (Rupees Twenty Two Thousand Six Hundred and Twenty only) plus GST 
as applicable, subject to income tax deduction at source at the applicable rates per month 
(“O&M Charges”) during the Sub-Lease Period for maintenance of the Demised 
Premises. For maintenance of the building, maintenance of common lobbies, landscaping, 
chillers, common toilets, lifts, diesel, stand-by generators, security at gate and main 
entrance, common electrical equipment, insurance, as more particularly set out in 
Schedule D, the Sub-Lessee will pay an amount of  Rs 1,500/- (Rupees Fifteen hundred 
only) (“Common Facilities Maintenance Charges” or “CFM Charges”) per month in 
addition to the O&M Charges. The Sub-Lessee agrees to pay Service Tax or any other 
future levies on the O&M Charges, if applicable. The O&M Charges and CFM Charges 
shall become payable in advance every month on or before 7th day of the English calendar 
month.  
(d) 
The O&M Charges will be reviewed on an annual basis and shall be revised based on 
increase in WPI, CPI and Minimum Wages as Gazette by Government which will be 
proportionately shared by all the occupants.  
(e) 
All indirect taxes such as GST or any other taxes levied by statutory authorities excluding 
property tax shall be payable by the Sub-Lessee. 
(f) 
The Sub-Lessee shall provide the Sub-Lessor with certificates reflecting the deduction of 
tax at source promptly as per the Income Tax Laws. 
ARTICLE.V- OBLIGATIONS OF THE PARTIES 
(a) 
The Sub-Lessee shall regularly pay the Rent reserved under this Deed and all the 
outgoings, and charges stipulated herein, within the time and in the manner herein 
provided. 
(b) 
The Sub-Lessee shall use the Demised Premises for any purposes related to conducting 
its commercial operations including without limitation IT consulting, global consulting, 
Investment management, Financial management etc. 
(c) 
The Sub-Lessee shall not store any hazardous or inflammable articles in the Demised 
Premises or in any proximity to the Demised Premises which could damage or harm 
persons or the Sub-Lessor’s property. 
(d) 
The Sub-Lessee shall be responsible for carrying out all minor, routine repairs. The Sub-
Lessor shall be responsible for carrying out all major repairs including but not limited to 
structural damages, damage to air conditioners, lifts, water sewage plant etc. The Sub-
Lessor, its authorized agents and employees shall have the right to enter upon the Demised 
Premises for inspection and carrying out repairs at reasonable working hours in the day 
with  prior written notice to the Sub-Lessee to enable the Sub-Lessee or its representative 
to be present so as to afford such entry. A prior written notice of 48 hours shall suffice 
and the Sub-Lessor shall ensure that it doesn’t interfere with or disturb the Sub-Lessee’s 
Page 6 of 23 
 
 
operations. If the Sub-Lessor fails to carry out major repairs promptly, the Sub-Lessee 
may carry them out and recover the cost thereof from the Sub-Lessor, including deducting 
such costs from the Rent payable for the Demised Premises. However, if the major repairs 
are caused due to negligence/mishandling by the Sub-Lessee the same shall be borne by 
the Sub-Lessee. 
(e) 
The Sub-Lessee shall have unlimited access to the Demised Premises twenty four (24) 
hours per day and seven (7) days per week, three hundred and sixty five (365) days a year 
of operations and support services, including electricity, water, power back up, 
rodent/vermin protection, security and lifts (collectively, the “Support Services”).

. The Sub-Lessor shall be responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the cafeteria.
